question: Where is the medulla oblongata located in the human body?

options.B: Inside the central part of the cerebellum
options.C: At the lowest part of the brainstem
options.D: At the very tip of the spinal cord

explanation: The medulla forms the inferior section of the brainstem, connecting the brain directly to the spinal cord. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T21#GNS211_U3_T21_h1)

question: Why is serious damage to the medulla oblongata so dangerous?

options.A: It coordinates voluntary muscle movement for walking
options.B: It stores long-term memory and learning skills
options.C: It produces cerebrospinal fluid for the brain
options.D: It controls basic functions that keep us alive

explanation: Because it houses vital control centers for breathing and heart rate, injury here quickly stops life-sustaining processes. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T21#GNS211_U3_T21_h1)

question: What are the prominent parallel ridges found on the front surface of the medulla called?
explanation: You got it! The pyramids are the distinct ridges on the front (anterior) surface of the medulla that carry important motor pathways down from the brain. Keep building that knowledge!

question: Which cranial nerves are attached to the medulla oblongata?

options.A: CN V, VI, VII, and VIII
options.B: CN IX, X, XI, and XII
options.C: CN III, IV, V, and VI
options.D: CN I, II, III, and IV

explanation: The glossopharyngeal, vagus, accessory, and hypoglossal cranial nerves all have their roots emerging from the medulla. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T21#GNS211_U3_T21_h2)

question: What is the decussation of the pyramids?

options.A: The fusion of the brainstem with the spinal cord
options.B: The crossing over of motor fibers to the opposite side
options.C: The production of fluid inside the brain ventricles
options.D: The separation of sensory nerves from motor nerves

explanation: Decussation simply means crossing over, which is why movement on one side of the body is controlled by the opposite brain hemisphere. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T21#GNS211_U3_T21_h3)

question: A patient suffers a stroke in the left motor cortex of the brain. Where will the resulting muscle weakness appear?

options.A: Only in the muscles of the face
options.B: On the right side of the body
options.C: Equally on both sides of the body
options.D: On the left side of the body

explanation: Because motor fibers cross at the medullary pyramids, damage to one side of the brain affects the contralateral side of the body. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T21#GNS211_U3_T21_h3)

question: What is the primary job of the respiratory center in the medulla?

options.A: Filtering dust and germs out of inhaled air
options.B: Setting the basic rhythm and depth of breathing
options.C: Exchanging oxygen across the lung membranes
options.D: Producing mucus to keep the airway moist

explanation: The medullary respiratory center automatically drives the inhale-and-exhale cycle without needing conscious thought. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T21#GNS211_U3_T21_h4)

question: How does the cardiovascular center in the medulla help regulate blood pressure?

options.A: By releasing digestive enzymes into the blood
options.B: By producing red blood cells in the bone marrow
options.C: By adjusting heart rate and blood vessel diameter
options.D: By filtering excess water out of the bloodstream

explanation: The cardiovascular center changes how fast the heart beats and how tightly blood vessels squeeze to keep blood pressure stable. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T21#GNS211_U3_T21_h4)

question: Which reflex is NOT coordinated by the medulla oblongata?

options.D: Visual tracking of a moving object

explanation: Visual tracking is handled by higher brain areas and midbrain structures, whereas vomiting, swallowing, and coughing are medullary reflexes. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T21#GNS211_U3_T21_h5)

question: Why are involuntary reflexes like coughing and vomiting important for survival?

options.A: They increase the amount of red blood cells in circulation
options.B: They cool down the body during a high fever
options.C: They protect the body from harmful substances and blockages
options.D: They help the digestive system absorb extra vitamins

explanation: These protective reflexes quickly expel irritants or foreign items from the airway and digestive tract to prevent injury. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T21#GNS211_U3_T21_h5)

question: A patient with a medullary stroke has a weak gag reflex and trouble swallowing. What is the most important nursing priority?

options.A: Checking passive range of motion in the limbs
options.B: Applying warm compresses to the neck muscles
options.C: Preventing food or liquid from entering the airway
options.D: Encouraging high fluid intake by mouth immediately

explanation: Impaired swallowing and a weak gag reflex lead straight to aspiration and pneumonia, making airway safety the primary concern. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T21#GNS211_U3_T21_h6)

question: Why must nurses monitor vital signs very closely in a patient with a suspected brainstem injury involving the medulla?

options.A: Cardiovascular and respiratory failure can happen suddenly
options.B: Kidney failure develops within the first hour
options.C: Blood pressure medications stop working entirely
options.D: Core body temperature always drops below normal

explanation: Because the medulla houses the primary breathing and heart rate centers, injury here directly threatens life support functions. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T21#GNS211_U3_T21_h6)
